title: Lever up a crate and slide dunnage under it
instruction: Press the red lever's handle down to lift the front of the blue crate and hold it there, slide the wooden block under the crate's raised front edge with the other arm, then let go of the lever so the crate rests on the block.
context: Freight and stock handlers (O*NET 53-7062.00) raise heavy crates with a pry lever to slip dunnage under them so a forklift or straps can get beneath. One arm must work the lever and keep the edge up while the other places the block: the crate is too wide to grip, and its edge drops back if the lever is let go first.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Crate: closed blue box, PLA shell weighted to 2 kg, 22 deep x 26 wide x 10 tall, front face at x 40 centred at y 0, with a lifting pocket 5 wide, 3.5 deep and 1.6 tall in the middle of its front bottom edge. Lever stand: dark grey, 2 kg, 7 x 9.6 cm footprint, pin 1 cm above the table at x 35.5, y 0, 4.5 cm in front of the crate. Lever: red, 200 g, 3.2 cm wide toe plate reaching 7.5 cm in front of the pin into the pocket; its handle bar rises 35 degrees back toward the arms to a 2.4 x 2.4 x 3.2 cm dark knob centred at x 16.9, 14.6 cm up. It turns 19 degrees down from rest. Block: light wood, 100 g, 12 x 3.6 x 1.4 cm, lying lengthwise along x centred at x 28, y 17.
scoring: Measured with a ruler on side and top photos. 0 if the crate's front edge ever moved 3 cm across the table, turned 10 degrees, tilted 10 degrees sideways or rose over 5 cm, or the lever stand moved 3 cm or turned 10 degrees. Otherwise: 1.0 if at the end the crate rests on the block (its underside on the block's top, front edge 1-3.2 cm up, the block flat with its front end 2.5-12 cm under the crate, within the crate's width) with the lever let go, still for 1 s; 0.75 if it rests on the block but the lever is still held down; 0.5 if the block was ever 2.5 cm or more under the front edge while that edge was 1.2 cm or more up; 0.25 if the front edge was lifted 1.2 cm or more; else 0.
reset_notes: Lift the crate's front edge with the lever, pull the block out, and let the crate down on its marked outline with the toe in its pocket. Put the lever stand and the block back on their marked outlines.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes. The lever is a revolute joint on its stand with a weak return spring (1.5 N m per rad, holding it on its rest stop) and a 19-degree lower stop. It lifts the crate only by contact between the toe and the pocket's roof; the crate pivots on its back edge. The crate and stand are loose and can be shoved or tipped. No contact force cap is enforced in simulation.
